elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: New clause inserted after 9.3: "Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor..." The contradicting bar in 2.1 was conformed to "without reduction rights," so the right is unconditional and operative during the three-year commitment.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor" - exactly 30 days, written, and no additional conditions or reminder mechanics attached.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "in which case Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees pro rata for the period after the effective date of termination" - the pro-rata basis is stated expressly, not merely inferred from a post-termination period.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: "Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a committed term." No retained Vendor convenience right elsewhere in Section 9 (9.1 breach, 9.2 insolvency, 9.3 Customer-only cause exits).

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted clause uses thirty days' notice, which sits below the 60-90 day fallback band; the fallback notice term is not rendered anywhere in operative text (only offered in the margin comment).

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the redline imposes no early-termination fee, penalty, or contingent payment on Customer's convenience exit, so there is no fee requiring a cap. Section 2.1's take-or-pay volume commitment is retained but is not framed as an early-termination fee.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply in substance: Vendor holds no convenience right at all, and the new sentence expressly bars Vendor convenience termination during a committed term, which is at least as protective as limiting it to term end. Section 8.2 non-renewal is natural-term expiry evaluated under RENEWAL.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no Vendor convenience termination right exists in the rendered document, so no Vendor notice period is required.

reasons: Preferred level is position-complete: all four preferred elements appear in operative language (30 days' written notice, express pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, Agreement-or-Order-Form scope, and an express bar on Vendor convenience termination during a committed term).

Fallback is incomplete only on the notice band (30 days rather than 60-90); this is immaterial because the preferred checklist is fully met, and the fallback is correctly offered in the comment rather than in the text.

Minimality holds: two operations only. The Section 2.1 edit deletes just the words "or termination" - necessary, because the retained "without reduction or termination rights" would otherwise contradict the new convenience right during the three-year commitment - and preserves the Customer-adverse but unrelated volume-reduction restriction and the take-or-pay figure. No survival tail, at-own-expense language, notice procedure, or other extras were added.

Intent preserved: 9.1-9.3 cause-based exits, 9.5's non-cross-termination and cumulative-remedies sentence, and the Section 20.5 cross-reference all survive without contradiction; no term is left undefined and no cross-reference dangles.

Drafting nit for the drafter (not a defect in substance): the inserted paragraph is unnumbered and sits between 9.3 and 9.5 - label it "9.4" as described in the margin comment so the section numbering is continuous.

Finding status "deviation" is correct: before the redline, Customer had no convenience exit across a three-year committed term and Section 2.1 affirmatively stripped termination rights, which is walk-away territory under T4C.
